security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are Markdown backticks, code fences, or TypeScript template literals, not shell execution. The real residual risks are npm/npx package execution, unpinned latest scaffolding, and a third-party CDN import. No prompt injection language was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Pin create-near-app to a reviewed version and require user approval before running npx or --install commands.

remediation.issue: npm install guidance for third-party wallet packages
remediation.suggestion: Document package version pins and advise users to inspect package metadata and lockfiles before installation.
Prefer npm with a lockfile, or pin the CDN package version and document integrity considerations.
Use testnet in beginner examples and reserve mainnet guidance for explicit production deployment steps.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to run npx create-near-app@latest and an install variant with --install. This can execute changing npm registry code and install dependencies without pinned versions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly use @latest and --install in shell commands. That combination creates clear supply-chain risk, even though the workflow is legitimate.

semantic_findings.title: Mainnet Examples Can Affect Real Assets
semantic_findings.description: Quick-start wallet examples set network to mainnet before showing contract calls and transfers. Copying this pattern can place user transactions on mainnet before testnet validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples use mainnet and later present write, transfer, and conversion helpers. The risk depends on user choices, so confidence is high enough to flag but not severe.

content.user_title: Build NEAR dApps With Wallet Support
content.value_statement: NEAR dApp setup requires wallet, contract, and transaction patterns across several libraries. This skill gives practical setup paths for scaffolding, React hooks, vanilla JavaScript, and common NEAR calls.
actual_capabilities: Guides new NEAR dApp scaffolding with create-near-app options.
Shows React wallet setup with NearProvider and useNearWallet.
Explains low-level wallet integration with NearConnector for non-React apps.
Provides examples for view calls, function calls, transfers, and transaction signing.
Covers NEAR and yoctoNEAR unit conversion patterns.
Lists package installation steps and framework choices.
limitations: Does not audit generated smart contracts or wallet libraries.
Depends on external npm packages and NEAR RPC services.
Examples require user review before mainnet transactions.
Does not replace official NEAR or package documentation.

use_cases.title: Add Wallet Login to React
use_cases.description: Integrate NEAR sign-in, sign-out, account state, and contract calls into an existing React application.

use_cases.title: Start a NEAR Prototype
use_cases.description: Create a new dApp scaffold with a selected frontend framework and smart contract language.

use_cases.title: Connect UI to Contracts
use_cases.description: Build user flows for read calls, write calls, deposits, transfers, and transaction signing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter dApp
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a NEAR dApp starter plan using Vite React and a Rust contract. Include the files to inspect before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add React Wallet Login
prompt_templates.prompt: Add NEAR wallet connection to my React app with near-connect-hooks. Show the provider placement, wallet state, and login button behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Build Contract Interaction UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a NEAR frontend flow for reading contract state and sending a wallet-approved function call with gas and deposit values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Advanced Wallet Transactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a non-React NEAR wallet integration using NearConnector, WalletConnect, transaction signing, and NEP-413 message signing.

output_examples.input: Add NEAR wallet login to an existing React app.
output_examples.output: A focused implementation plan covering package review, provider setup, wallet state, sign-in controls, and testnet verification.

output_examples.input: Create a new NEAR prototype with a frontend and contract.
output_examples.output: A scaffold plan with framework and contract choices, command approval notes, generated project structure, and next validation steps.

output_examples.input: Connect a UI button to a NEAR contract method.
output_examples.output: A transaction flow that names the contract, method, arguments, gas, deposit, wallet approval step, and expected user feedback.

best_practices: Start on testnet and verify contract names, methods, gas, and deposits before mainnet use.
Pin package versions and review install commands before allowing an agent to run them.
Show clear transaction details to users before wallet approval.
anti_patterns: Running npx latest or install commands without user approval.
Hardcoding mainnet settings before testnet validation.
Treating wallet sign-in as authorization for privileged app actions.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build NEAR dApps with project scaffolding, wallet connection, contract calls, transfers, and transaction signing patterns.

faq.question: Does it support existing React apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a path for adding NearProvider, useNearWallet, sign-in, sign-out, and contract helpers to React apps.

faq.question: Can it support non-React apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes direct NearConnector guidance for vanilla JavaScript or other frontend frameworks.

faq.question: Does it deploy smart contracts?
faq.answer: No. It can guide scaffold and frontend workflows, but deployment choices must be reviewed in the generated project.

faq.question: Should commands be run automatically?
faq.answer: No. npx and npm commands should be reviewed, pinned where possible, and approved before execution.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
